data.title: All Americans Are Feeling Squeezed. The Reactions Are Just Different. — Barrons.com
data.description:
By Teresa Rivas

In response to F. Scott Fitzgerald's assertion that the rich are very different from regular folk, Earnest Hemingway replied, "Yes, they have more money." Or so the story goes.

That money only goes so far, however, when prices rise incessantly.

There has been plenty written about the K-shaped economy, where high- and low-income earners feel dramatically differently about their spending power. Yet it seems that nearly all Americans across the income spectrum are feeling the pinch of persistently higher gas prices on top of years of inflation. They're just handling it in different ways.

Consumers are unhappy with price increases, and still retail sales climb higher and higher even when adjusted for inflation. With the job market holding relatively steady, there haven't been major pullbacks in consumer spending.

However, wages haven't kept up the pace with inflation in recent months, writes LPL Chief Economist Jeffrey Roach. That impacts lower-earning Americans more, since they have less of a financial cushion. But even those in a position to splash out aren't inclined to do so, Roach notes.

"Households say jobs are harder to find, expect weaker income six months from now, and see business conditions deteriorating. Fewer openings and tougher job-hunting have people feeling as gloomy as they did in early 2021...plans to buy a home, a vehicle, or a major appliance have declined from prior months."

Holiday shopping intentions tell a similar story.

A survey by Teneo found that lower- and middle-income households plan to cut their holiday spending by at least 20%. Higher-income earners, who have theoretically enjoyed healthy stock market gains, are planning to hold their spending steady. That is better than slashing budgets, but not as ebullient as expected. A majority of respondents across income cohorts said they were looking for deals. Value is key.

New research by Bernstein analyst Zhihan Mausing, who used traffic and demographic data from Advan, shows more of the same: Both high- and low-income Americans have changed their habits.

"The short answer is that low income consumers are shopping more frequently - with smaller baskets - in value channels (especially in nearby dollar stores to save on gas)," she writes. "Meanwhile, for higher income consumers who can afford to buy larger baskets online, they are likely turning more to e-commerce rather than trading down in the brick and mortar channel amid ongoing gas inflation."

Ma found that visits to Walmart remained in the mid-single digit range despite a modest slowdown "perhaps as elevated gas prices weigh on lower income customers' willingness to drive to a Walmart," she posits.

If higher gas prices relent, that could be a catalyst for growth for Walmart and other retailers no matter which income band they cater to.

Costco Wholesale, which tends to cater to shoppers higher up the income scale, saw its visits accelerate in the second and third quarter, likely driven by its cheaper gas offerings.

"Target showed the strongest sequential improvement, with visits growth accelerating to the high-single digit range...supported by Target's improved merchandising and in-store experience," she writes. Target is in the midst of a turnaround focused on bringing shoppers back with better merchandising that has helped it sidestep some of the broader retail pain this year.

Visits to Dollar Tree and Dollar General are both positive year over year, although the latter has seen its traffic decelerate throughout the year. However she cautions that investors shouldn't extrapolate too much from this, given Dollar General's expanding partnerships with DoorDash, UberEats and Instacart. Inflationary pressure has been a double-edged sword for these deep discounters. Higher prices have weighed on core, lower-income consumers, while leading to some higher-income shoppers trading down.

"Overall, the U.S. consumer has remained resilient but value seeking," Ma concludes. "Should gas inflation start to moderate, this could weigh on dollar stores' traffic but help basket size, while Walmart could see improved in-store traffic as people are more inclined to drive."

When gas prices — currently around $4.30, near spring highs — start to moderate is anyone's guess.

Write to Teresa Rivas at teresa.rivas@barrons.com

data.title: Brazilian assets rise as investors await pivotal election
data.description:
Key points:
  • Brazilian assets steady ahead of Sunday election
  • Colombia peso up nearly 1%, government cuts spending budget
  • Venezuelans call for elections in first national protest in nearly two years
  • Mexican economy exceeds expectations in August

By Sudeshna Ghoshal and Johann M Cherian

Brazilian stocks rose on Friday as investors geared up for the presidential runoff in Latin America's largest economy, while the currency hit its highest in more than a week.

Voters will decide between right-wing candidate Senator Flavio Bolsonaro and incumbent President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva on Sunday. Bolsonaro had performed better than expected earlier in the month, but recent polls have shown his lead over Lula was narrowing, sparking volatility in local markets.

The real has rallied 3.4% this month, marking its biggest monthly gain since April, while local stocks have advanced 10.3%, on course for their strongest month since January, on expectations that the senator would adopt fiscal consolidation policies if he won.

However, analysts said he was yet to offer clarity on the subject.

On Friday, the currency rose 0.9% against the dollar, while stocks were little changed. International bonds (105756CN8=), (105756BY5=) were marginally higher, while the equity benchmark rose 0.6%.

Ahead of the vote, data showed consumer inflation rose less-than-expected in the month to mid-October.

"Brazil is at the verge of fiscal dominance dynamics, and anything that improves the fiscal situation can lower risk premia," said Alejandro Cuadrado, managing director, global head FX & LatAm Strategy at BBVA.

"Lower risk premia implies the central bank can find more room to cut, lower interest rates, imply better valuations for Brazilian equities and potential growth and that brings flows from the offshore into Brazil."

MSCI indexes tracking regional equities (.MILA00000PUS) and currencies (.MILA00000CUS) rose 1.2% and 0.6%, respectively.

Brent crude prices rose over 3% after Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia stoked concerns over further disruption to energy supplies from the Middle East.

Oil exporter Colombia's peso appreciated the most among regional currencies. It was last up nearly 1% after hitting a near one-month high.

Public finances were also in focus as the country's government cut this year's spending budget by 13.8 trillion pesos ($4.33 billion), although it was smaller than previously announced.

The Mexican peso inched up 0.2% against the dollar, but eyed its seventh straight week of losses, hit by expectations of a narrowing of the US-Mexico interest rate differential and uncertainty over the USMCA free trade deal.

Data showed the region's second largest economy grew more than expected in August from the prior month, with all three main sectors posting gains, official data showed.

Elsewhere, Venezuelans took to the streets on Thursday in the first nationwide opposition protest in nearly two years, as demonstrators demanded free elections and other political changes, with a notably thin presence of security forces.

The country's legacy international maturities were marginally higher.

Meanwhile, US first lady Melania Trump secured a ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine in the Russian-controlled city of Oleshky, which will begin on October 29, the White House said.

Kyiv's hard currency bonds (XS2895057334=TE), (XS2895056369=TE) gained over a cent following the news.

data.title: Former LPL Advisor Pleads Guilty to Fraud in Scheme That Cost Firms $3.3 Million — Barrons.com
data.description:
By Kenneth Corbin

A barred former investment advisor and broker has pleaded guilty to wire fraud in connection with a scheme that prosecutors say cost three financial services companies more than $3.3 million. Andrew Komarow, 37, of Avon, Conn., had initially pleaded not guilty to 11 charges, but entered a guilty plea to a lone count in federal court on Thursday.

Reached by email, Komarow didn't immediately provide a comment on the case. His lawyer didn't immediately respond to a request for comment.

Prosecutors say the fraud occurred between October 2022 and February 2023, when Komarow obtained lines of credit from three financial services companies and initiated nearly $9 million worth of transfers from his bank accounts to various brokerage accounts in his name. He executed those transactions knowing that he didn't have sufficient funds to support the transfers.

Komarow exploited a delay in the time between initiating those transfers and when the financial services firms posted and cleared them. He would then "conduct high-risk, short-term options trading in an attempt to make immediate profits to cover his insufficient funds," according to the Justice Department.

The financial services firms lost $3.35 million through the scheme, prosecutors say.

Komarow, who has autism, had been a widely cited expert on issues around neurodiversity and wealth management. He had been involved with the Financial Planning Association's efforts to support neurodivergent advisors and founded Planning Across the Spectrum, a now-defunct wealth management firm focused on special-needs planning.

Komarow first registered as a broker in 2010 with Pruco Securities and moved to LPL Financial in 2016. Later that year he registered as an investment advisor with Private Advisory Group, a large advisor firm affiliated with LPL.

By late 2022, the companies he worked for had caught on to Komarow's money-transfer scheme. Private Advisory Group terminated him in November of that year and LPL cut him loose in December, according to registration records.

Komarow was also on the radar of state and federal regulators. Finra, the brokerage industry's self-regulatory authority, barred Komarow from associating with any broker in June 2023. Connecticut securities regulators barred him from the industry in January 2024, and the Securities and Exchange Commission barred him in February 2024.

In the criminal case, the wire fraud charge carries a maximum sentence of 20 years in prison. The court hasn't scheduled Komarow's sentencing.

data.title: CVS is trying out pharmacists in chronic health management
data.description:
By Caroline Humer

CVS Health Chief Medical Officer Dr. Amy Compton-Phillips on Friday said healthcare affordability and access could potentially improve if pharmacists in its 9,000 retail stores play a bigger role in chronic disease management, helping consumers stay on top of their most important health metrics.

Each year, millions of Americans die from heart attacks, strokes, kidney disease, diabetes and other chronic conditions that can be treated with medical attention and proper medicines, she said.

"We want to make it really easy and convenient for you to know your numbers," she said, adding that the company is experimenting with how pharmacists could become more involved by taking measurements for blood pressure, cholesterol, and blood sugar.

CVS is starting now with a pilot in five stores in Michigan to try out the concept, she said. In the US, the role of pharmacists is determined in part by varying state pharmacy regulations.

CVS Health is one of the largest US healthcare conglomerates, with the Aetna health insurance company, CVS Caremark pharmacy benefit manager and a nationwide network of retail pharmacies under its corporate umbrella.

Compton-Phillips, speaking during the Reuters Total Health conference in Nashville, said the company was also talking to the government's Medicare agency about the role pharmacists could play in expanding access to healthcare and providing lower-cost healthcare.

Affordability of healthcare is a key issue for the Trump administration, which is experimenting with different pilots that could lower costs for the more than 70 million people enrolled in the Medicare program for people aged 65 and older or with disabilities.

One of the pilots involves more access to highly popular GLP-1 medications used to treat obesity, which the government has made available for $50 a month for a limited time through TrumpRx.gov.

More companies, however, are cutting corporate coverage of the medicines in 2027, recent surveys show, concerned about the increased cost to their health plans for the Eli Lilly and Novo Nordisk medicines such as Mounjaro, Zepbound, Ozempic and Wegovy.

Those medicines cost a few hundred dollars on the drugmakers' direct-pay websites, but can be more expensive to employers when they are covered in their insurance plans.

Compton-Phillips said she would like to see better access to the GLP-1 drugs at a lower cost, describing their potential health benefits as "incredible."

"They really do have real benefits in decreasing heart disease and kidney disease," she said.

"I can't wait until 2032," she said. "That's when Ozempic goes generic in the US and I think we are going to be writing prescriptions for it like water."

data.title: CFTC data shows Bitcoin futures speculators net long 2,418 contracts
data.description:
Large speculators in CME Bitcoin futures held a net long position of 2,418 contracts for the week of October 20, 2026, according to the Commodity Futures Trading Commission's latest Commitments of Traders report.

That is a slight pullback from the prior week's 2,534 contracts.

The report, released October 23, also showed speculators paring bets against most US Treasury futures. Meanwhile, the euro sat deep in net short territory.

The CFTC publishes its Commitments of Traders, or COT, data every Friday at 3:30 p.m. ET. Each release reflects positions as of the preceding Tuesday.

The 2,418-contract figure covers non-commercial speculators in CME Bitcoin futures. It blends standard and micro contracts under the legacy reporting format.

A standard CME Bitcoin contract represents 5 BTC, while a micro contract represents just 0.1 BTC.

For context, the week ending October 13 showed large speculators net long 2,534 contracts, with total open interest of 20,752 contracts. Open interest measures the total number of outstanding contracts that have not been closed out.

The more granular Traders in Financial Futures breakdown told a split story for that October 13 week. Leveraged funds, a category that typically includes hedge funds, were net short roughly 5,844 standard contracts.

Asset managers and institutions, by contrast, were net long 3,642 contracts.

The broader report showed a fairly consistent theme in the bond market: speculators trimming short positions.

  • Speculators cut their net short in CBOT US 2-year Treasury futures by 54,796 contracts to 856,783.
  • Net shorts in 5-year Treasury futures fell by 6,095 contracts to 1,074,109.
  • Net shorts in 10-year Treasury futures dropped by 23,809 contracts to 964,293.
  • Net shorts in CBOT US Treasury bond futures shrank by 58,019 contracts to 68,419.

The lone exception was the long end. Speculators increased their net short in UltraBond Treasury futures by 53,564 contracts to 375,161.

Equity fund speculators trimmed their S&P 500 CME net short by 42,221 contracts to 348,674.

Equity fund managers cut their S&P 500 CME net long by 18,079 contracts to 894,464.

In currencies, the euro held a net short position of 134,524 contracts.

The COT report has an important limitation. It tells you what traders hold, not why they hold it, and it makes no attempt to forecast prices.

A net long can reflect outright bullish conviction. It can also be one leg of a hedged trade, such as a basis trade where a fund buys spot exposure and sells futures to capture the price gap between them.

That caveat is especially relevant to the Bitcoin data. The October 13 split, with leveraged funds net short and asset managers net long, is consistent with a market where some participants are hedging rather than simply calling direction.

The next COT report is anticipated on October 30, 2026. Traders watching Bitcoin will want to see whether open interest holds near the 20,752-contract level recorded for October 13, and whether speculators keep inching back from their net long or start adding again.

data.title: After previous day's slump, trading is quieter among AI shares
data.description:
Key points:
  • Nasdaq little changed Friday after Thursday selloff
  • Microsoft, Alphabet, Amazon due to report next week
  • Market volatility centers on AI activity

By Caroline Valetkevitch

Big AI stocks were mixed on Friday, a day after the biggest decline in the Nasdaq Composite Index in four months, giving investors a welcome respite as they look forward to more information on Anthropic's forthcoming IPO and a further wave of earnings over the next week.

Meta Platforms , the center of Thursday's storm, was fractionally lower following Thursday's 7% decline. The operator of social media networks and major AI investor said in its earnings report this week that it would create a new class of shares in part to raise money for further capital spending, which was taken as evidence that the next leg of the AI buildout will be costly for shareholders.

Other major AI players were mixed on Friday, with SpaceX , Oracle and Dell Technologies up 1% to 2% and Nvidia , Alphabet and Amazon down less than 1%. Big semiconductor stocks were mostly higher after their largest decline since the summer on Thursday.

Credit default swaps tracking the perceived risk of default at the biggest AI players were mostly modestly lower, with Meta's five-year CDS spread trading 0.3% narrower at 123, according to LSEG data. The swaps enable investors to bet on a default using contracts typically with terms of five or 10 years, though contracts frequently change hands for the purposes of hedging positions and betting on near-term market moves.

Thursday's deluge and the day-after calm is the latest sign of indirection in a market that has hovered near record highs without breaking out, said Rick Meckler, partner at Cherry Lane Investments, a family investment office in New Vernon, New Jersey.

"To some extent, we're seeing the market tread water over a longer period of time because every sell-off has been met by buyers and every point upward has been met by sellers," Meckler said.

The Nasdaq was barely changed on Friday afternoon.

Credit-default swap premiums, reflecting the annual cost borne by the swap purchaser in thousands of dollars, have risen over the past year with concern about the risks being taken on by large AI spenders. The premiums rose on Thursday after Meta's decision to sell more stock, as much of the buildout to date has been financed through debt issuance.

The concerns around AI spending and investment returns have added to the market's volatility since Treasury yields rose sharply in August, which changed the economics of investing and bond issuance, given the increasing attractiveness of a higher risk-free rate.

It's been "a very volatile week," said Art Hogan, chief market strategist at B Riley Wealth in Boston. "There's no doubt at some point in time that the higher inflation moves, especially if driven by unsustainably higher energy prices ... would have to show up in corporate earnings. It hasn't yet, but that's the concern. And market participants are trying to position for that."

Shares of neoclouds, smaller companies tied to AI data centers and other infrastructure projects like CoreWeave , have dropped due to anxiety over their future. Their performance of late has also raised talk on Wall Street that capital is growing scarce - which stands to raise costs further and potentially raise funding issues down the road.

Even so, many investors remain positive on the sector, where giant AI lab Anthropic is expected to publish its IPO prospectus in coming days and Alphabet, Amazon and Microsoft are expected to report earnings next week.

"In general, AI news in terms of revenues continues to be very strong, it's just at what cost and how long that growth is sustainable," Meckler said. "We really haven't gotten to the point of the market sort of focusing on winners and losers. It's been one big sector trade every day."

data.title: Franklin Templeton to launch two 95% stock, 5% Bitcoin ETFs
data.description:
Franklin Templeton plans to launch two exchange-traded funds that put 95% of their assets in US stocks and 5% in Bitcoin. One is built around S&P 500 exposure. The other targets the Nasdaq 100.

The asset manager filed a Form 8-A with the SEC on October 22, 2026. That filing typically signals a listing is close.

The two products are the Franklin US Equity Bitcoin DRIP Index ETF, ticker FBEQ, and the Franklin US Innovation Bitcoin DRIP Index ETF, ticker FIBT. Both will list on Nasdaq.

The effective date is projected for October 27, 2026. Trading is positioned to begin after that.

Under the hood, FBEQ tracks the VettaFi US Large-Cap 500 Bitcoin DRIP Index. FIBT follows the VettaFi US Innovation 100 Bitcoin DRIP Index.

"DRIP" refers to dividend reinvestment. Normally, an investor collects stock dividends and rolls them back into more shares. These funds route those payouts into Bitcoin instead.

The funds will not hold Bitcoin directly. They will get their exposure through exchange-traded products, including Franklin's existing spot Bitcoin ETF, EZBC.

The 5% Bitcoin allocation is a starting point, not a fixed ceiling. The Bitcoin weight can drift above 5% between rebalances, whether from dividend inflows or price gains.

Every quarter, the index trims the Bitcoin position back down to 4.5%. There is also a hard cap of 20% on Bitcoin's weight.

On cost, the research shows expense ratios reported as low as 0.09%.

These funds build on infrastructure Franklin already has. Its spot Bitcoin ETF, EZBC, has drawn approximately $335 million in net inflows.

EZBC now gets a second job as the Bitcoin engine inside these new equity funds.

FIBT deserves a closer look on one front. Growth-oriented, tech-heavy companies often pay smaller dividends than broad large-cap names, so the Bitcoin accumulation engine may run slower there than in FBEQ.

The quarterly trim cuts the other way. When Bitcoin outperforms, the index sells some of it back down to 4.5%, so these funds will not be pure buy-and-hold vehicles for the asset.

The launch timeline puts the answer in the hands of the market fairly soon after October 27, 2026.
